final_answer: Fixed the single-decimal bug in `parse_amount` in `ledger/money.py`: the fractional part is now padded to two digits before conversion, so `10.5` books 1050 cents instead of 1005. The existing tests pass, and spot checks confirm `10.5`, `10.50`, `10`, `10.`, `0.5`, and `-3.07` all parse correctly. Public names and signatures are unchanged.

I added `Journal.entries_for`, `reports.register`, and `reports.format_register` as specified, with an unknown account raising `ValueError`. I also added a `test_register` test covering net per-entry amounts, same-day ordering, running balances across the `start`/`end` filter, and the formatted output; all 4 tests pass.

All five error cases now raise their own `LedgerError` subclasses, and each also inherits `ValueError`. The new `ImportRowError` carries `line` and `cause`, is raised from `import_csv` with the original error chained, and rows before the failure stay posted. No `raise ValueError` remains in `ledger/`, and the 9 tests pass with the updated and new cases in `tests/test_ledger.py`.

The nearest-rank bug was in `percentile` in `logkit/stats.py`, which used a floor index without the `-1`. It now computes `ceil(p * n / 100) - 1` and clamps to the valid range, so p95 of 1..20 gives 19 and p50 of 1,2,3,4 gives 2. I added those cases to `tests/test_logkit.py`, and all 3 tests pass.

All three features are in: `--since` and `--until` (inclusive and exclusive, via `filters.between`), `--json` (with `--summary` taking precedence), and `render.json_line`. Timestamps without a UTC offset, and bad or missing values, return 2 with a message on stderr. The full suite passes (11 tests), including a new `tests/test_cli.py` covering the bounds, combinations, error cases, and JSON key order.

`Record` is now a dataclass in `logkit/record.py`, and `parse_line` and `read_records` return it. `filters`, `stats`, and `cli` use attribute access, and `count_by` looks up the attribute by name with `getattr`. The four tests pass (I added a `count_by` test), and the CLI's `--summary` and `--level`/`--component` output matched the expected results on a sample log. The only remaining bracket access is in `render.table`, which indexes its own summary rows rather than log records, so I left it alone.

The bug was in `shop/pricing.py`: `total()` passed the pre-discount subtotal to `tax_for`, so every coupon left tax computed on the full price. It now taxes `subtotal − discount`, and the total is computed from that same taxable amount. I added a regression test for a $100 California order with SAVE10 (tax $6.52, total $96.52), and all 5 tests pass.

All four features are in: the `BUY2GET1:<sku>` coupon, the `"coupon"` key on orders, the `Discount (CODE)` receipt line, and the `--coupon` CLI override with usage errors returning 2. I added tests for each, and the full suite passes (10 tests).

`shop/` now uses integer cents throughout: `Item.price_cents`, `RATES_BP` in basis points, integer discount and tax rounding, `money(cents)`, and the CLI reads `price_cents`. The five tests pass (I also added a SAVE10 case), and a grep finds no `float`, `round(`, or decimal literals left in `shop/`.

The off-by-one was in `should_retry` in `taskq/retry.py`, which used `<=` and so allowed one extra attempt. I changed it to `<`, so a job with `max_attempts=3` now runs exactly three times before being marked dead. The existing test suite passes (3 tests).

Job dependencies are in place across `taskq/jobs.py`, `queue.py`, and `store.py`. `enqueue` validates `depends_on` and `pop_ready` waits for every dependency to be `"done"`. A `fail` that kills a job marks all queued transitive dependents dead with `dependency failed: <id>`, and dumps round-trip `depends_on` while old dumps load with an empty list. All 8 tests pass, including 5 new ones covering blocking, unknown IDs, transitive cascade, retry behaviour, and legacy loads.

One gap the spec doesn't cover: if you enqueue a job whose dependency is already `"dead"`, it stays queued forever because the cascade only runs at the moment of `fail`. Say if you want that case to kill the new job immediately.

The job statuses are now a `Status` enum in `taskq/jobs.py`, and `queue.py`, `worker.py` and `store.py` use its members, so the plain status strings appear only in `jobs.py`. `store.dump` still writes the plain string and `store.load` converts it back, and `stats()` still returns plain-string keys. The three tests pass, and I extended one to check that the status comes back as `Status.DONE` after a round trip.

The bug was the greedy bold pattern in `wiki/inline.py`: `\*\*(.+)\*\*` matched from the first `**` to the last. I changed it to the lazy `\*\*(.+?)\*\*`, so `**a** and **b**` now produces two separate `<strong>` spans. I also added a regression test, `test_two_bold_spans`, and the full suite passes (4 tests).

All three features are in: ordered lists, a `[TOC]` block that lists every heading, and unique heading ids (`intro`, `intro-2`, `intro-3`). The `<hN>` ids, TOC links and `toc.build` all use the same slugs. The test suite passes (6 tests), including new tests for each feature and the unique-id case.

The tuple blocks are now `Heading`, `Para`, `ListBlock` and `Code` dataclasses in `wiki/blocks.py`, and `html.render` and `toc.build` dispatch on them with `isinstance`. Unknown block types raise `ValueError("unknown block: ...")`. The five tests pass, including new ones for parse types and unknown blocks, and no `"heading"`, `"para"`, `"list"` or `"code"` strings remain in `wiki/`. `toc.build` still returns `(level, text, slug)` tuples because the request covered only block tuples.
